title: Uniformizer perturbations on completed monomial quotients
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $C$ be a Cohen ring with uniformizer $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively, which is sharp: $0$ is its only invertible element. Let $n\ge0$, put $S=C[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, where $C[P]=\bigoplus_{q\in P}Cz^q$ and $z^qz^r=z^{q+r}$, and put
$$J_S=(z^q\ (q\ne0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)S,\qquad \mathfrak a=(p)+J_S,\qquad B=\varprojlim_m S/\mathfrak a^m,\qquad J=J_SB.$$
The inverse limit is the adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For any monoid ideal $I\subseteq P$, meaning $I+P\subseteq I$ and allowing $I=\varnothing$ and $I=P$, put $IS=(z^q:q\in I)S$ and $N=B/(IS)B$. For every integer $m\ge0$, the natural map induces an isomorphism of $C$-modules
$$S/(IS+J_S^{m+1})\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ N/J^{m+1}N.$$
These modules are free of finite rank over $C$, and $\bigcap_{m\ge0}J^mN=0$. For every $\theta\in B$ with $\theta-p\in J$, multiplication by $\theta$ on $N$ is injective.

proof.text: By the Cohen-ring definition, $C$ is a principal ideal domain, $p\ne0$, and $C\to\varprojlim_k C/p^kC$ is bijective. The PID Noetherianity statement makes $C$ Noetherian. Choose nonzero generators $q_1,\ldots,q_d$ of $P$, omitting $0$ from a finite generating set (allow $d=0$). Sending polynomial generators to $z^{q_i}$ and $t_j$ gives a surjection $C[X_1,\ldots,X_d,T_1,\ldots,T_n]\to S$, since every basis monomial is a product of those generators. Thus the finite-type Noetherianity statement makes $S$ Noetherian. Every ideal $K\subseteq S$ is therefore finitely generated, by the definition of Noetherian; $S/K$ is cyclic.

source.place: Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence) and 0327 (definition-cohen-ring); the finite polynomial presentation is explicit.

proof.text: Write $e_{q,\alpha}=z^qt^\alpha$, for $(q,\alpha)\in P\times\mathbf N^n$; these form the displayed coefficient basis of $S$. A monomial-generated ideal is exactly the $C$-span of the basis monomials divisible by one of its generators: multiplication shifts indices, and conversely every such basis monomial is the generator times a monomial. Hence $IS$ is spanned by indices with $q\in I$, while $J_S^{m+1}$ is spanned by products of $m+1$ generators of $J_S$, times arbitrary monomials. Put $Q_m=S/(IS+J_S^{m+1})$. The images of the basis monomials outside this union of supports form a $C$-basis of $Q_m$, since quotienting a free coefficient module by a subset of its basis leaves precisely the complementary basis. This basis is finite: represent $q=\sum_i e_iq_i$; if $\sum_i e_i+\sum_j\alpha_j\ge m+1$, then $z^qt^\alpha\in J_S^{m+1}$. Thus every surviving index is the image of an exponent tuple of total degree at most $m$ in the finite list of $d+n$ generators. In particular each $Q_m$ is finite free, and multiplication by the nonzero $p\in C$ on it is injective.

source.place: ILO VI 1.6(ii), printed p.70, completed monoid algebra notation; elementary coefficient calculation for the extracted sublemma.

proof.text: For any ideal $K\subseteq S$, complete $0\to K\to S\to S/K\to0$ at $\mathfrak a$. All three modules are finite by Step 1, so exact completion gives a surjection $B\to\widehat{S/K}$ with kernel the image of $\widehat K\to B$. The finite-module tensor comparison identifies $\widehat K$ with $B\otimes_SK$. Its formula and naturality identify the latter map with $b\otimes k\mapsto bk$; its image is exactly $KB$, since tensors are finite sums of pure tensors and $KB$ consists of finite sums $bk$. We have therefore constructed a canonical $B$-linear isomorphism $B/KB\cong\widehat{S/K}=\varprojlim_r(S/K)/\mathfrak a^r(S/K)$, carrying the image of $s\in S$ to its compatible residue classes. All module actions in this identification are componentwise, as in the cited statements.

For fixed $m$, let $\overline J$ denote the action of $J_S$ on $Q_m$, so $\overline J^{m+1}Q_m=0$. Expanding products from $\mathfrak a=(p)+J_S$ shows, for every $k\ge0$, $p^kQ_m\subseteq\mathfrak a^kQ_m$ and $\mathfrak a^{k+m+1}Q_m\subseteq p^kQ_m$: a term with at least $m+1$ factors in $J_S$ vanishes, and every other term has at least $k$ factors $p$. The finite basis in Step 2 and completeness of $C$ give $Q_m\cong\varprojlim_k Q_m/p^kQ_m$ coefficient by coefficient. Explicitly, from compatible classes modulo $\mathfrak a^r$, take the class at $r=k+m+1$ modulo $p^k$ and recover a unique vector $x\in Q_m$ by that coefficient completeness. For fixed $r$, using $k\ge r$ shows that $x$ has the prescribed class modulo $\mathfrak a^r$. If a vector maps to zero modulo every $\mathfrak a^r$, the second inclusion puts it in every $p^kQ_m$, so all its coefficients are zero. Thus the canonical map $Q_m\to\widehat{Q_m}$ is bijective.

source.place: Tag 0327 (definition-cohen-ring), completeness clause; elementary comparison of the two explicit filtrations and finite coefficient limits.

proof.text: Apply Step 3 to $K=IS+J_S^{m+1}$ and Step 4 to identify $B/(IS+J_S^{m+1})B$ with $Q_m$, inversely to the map induced by $S\to B$. Extension of ideals respects sums and products directly from their finite-sum definitions, so $(IS+J_S^{m+1})B=(IS)B+J^{m+1}$. The maps sending the class of $b$ to its class in $(B/(IS)B)/J^{m+1}(B/(IS)B)$, and back, are mutually inverse. Consequently $Q_m\to N/J^{m+1}N$ is the asserted natural $C$-module isomorphism, proving also the finite-free assertion of the item.

source.place: Tags 00MA and 00MB, as already applied in Step 3; elementary quotient identifications.

proof.text: Apply Step 3 instead to $K=IS$ and put $M=S/IS$. It identifies $N$ with the actual module of compatible classes $\varprojlim_rM/\mathfrak a^rM$. For each $r$, the image in $B$ of every $j\in J_S$ acts as zero on the $r$th quotient after any product of $r$ such factors, since $J_S^r\subseteq\mathfrak a^r$. Finite sums with coefficients in $B$ give the same vanishing for every element of $J^rN$. Therefore an element of $\bigcap_rJ^rN$ has zero $r$th coordinate for every $r$, and is the zero compatible sequence. This proves the claimed $J$-adic separatedness without assuming that $J$ is a maximal ideal.

source.place: Tag 00MA, as already applied in Step 3; direct use of the componentwise inverse-limit description.

proof.text: Write $\theta=p+j$ with $j\in J$, and suppose $\theta x=0$ in $N$. Induct on $r\ge0$ to prove $x\in J^rN$. The case $r=0$ is automatic. If $x\in J^rN$, then $px=-jx\in J^{r+1}N$. By Step 5 with $m=r$, the quotient $N/J^{r+1}N$ is a free $C$-module, so multiplication by $p$ is injective on it, as checked in Step 2. Thus $x\in J^{r+1}N$. Step 6 now gives $x=0$. Applying this kernel calculation to $x-y$ proves injectivity of multiplication by $\theta$. If $I=P$ the module is zero and all the same arguments hold with the empty basis; $I=\varnothing$, $P=\{0\}$, $n=0$ and $m=0$ require no exclusions.

Step 1: the finite polynomial presentation makes S Noetherian. Step 2: the monomial-ideal support calculation gives a finite complementary C-basis; finiteness follows because z^q t^α lies in J_S^{m+1} once its total degree in the d+n generators is at least m+1. Step 3: B/KB ≅ (S/K)^ follows from the two completion statements, and naturality of c with c_S(b⊗s)=bs makes the image of K^ exactly KB. Step 4: p^kQ ⊆ 𝔞^kQ and 𝔞^{k+m+1}Q ⊆ p^kQ, and both directions of the bijection Q_m → Q_m^ are verified. Step 5: ι_{Q_m} is bijective, and KB=(IS)B+J^{m+1}. Step 6: the r-th coordinate of anything in J^rN vanishes, so the intersection is 0. Step 7: the induction is correct, using p injective on the C-free truncation. Edge cases tested: I=P, I=∅, I={≥2} in P=N (C[[z]]/(z^2)), m=0, and P={0} with n=0. No duplicate found by rg -L over dag/nodes for monomial/monoid-completion candidates. Details are in review.md.
